PullRequest.Title: Finish browser state cleanup after native page closure
PullRequest.Body:
Avoid an unhandled main-process error when Electron has already cleared a browser view's WebContents during native closure. Guard the native close call so registered cleanup still completes.

Strengthen the existing popup lifecycle smoke test to catch the reported disposal exception after restart.

Fixes #320443

Scenarios.Scenario: Native browser popup/page is closed by Electron, including during application restart, and its BrowserView receives the destroyed event after Electron has cleared WebContentsView.webContents.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Electron emits `destroyed`, `BrowserView.dispose()` detaches debugger state, removes the child view when possible, fires close observers that release the session/map/group references, checks the captured webContents, and disposes registered listeners. The changed guard prevents an exception and does not add work to this closure path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Detach the existing Electron debugger transport during `BrowserViewDebugger.dispose()`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once for each disposed view.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same debugger detachment occurred before the changed webContents access.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously before the BrowserView close event can complete, as it did before the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Remove the WebContentsView from the host window and, when webContents still exists and is live, request native WebContents closure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one removal and one close request per disposed view.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same removal and close request existed; accessing an already-cleared webContents threw before registered-disposable cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These native Electron operations remain on the disposal path; when Electron has already cleared webContents, the changed branch skips the close request instead of throwing.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One disposal per native browser view; a restart can dispose all currently open views, but the changed work remains one property capture and one null check per view.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Disposals are driven by Electron lifecycle events per view with no new queue or parallel fan-out introduced by the diff. Existing close observers perform per-view cleanup.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache lookup or population is involved. Cold and warm behavior are identical.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed hunk and destroyed listener directly establish the disposal path and one-per-view cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneously open browser views varies, but the diff adds only constant-time guarding per view and eliminates exceptional control flow.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change improves cleanup completion without adding repeated work, retention, boundary fan-out, or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Explicit destruction of a live browser view through BrowserViewMainService.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `destroyBrowserView()` deletes and disposes the map entry, then `BrowserView.dispose()` performs the existing debugger detach, native view removal, close notification, native webContents close, and registered-listener cleanup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Destroy a BrowserView through the existing service boundary and close its Electron webContents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One service disposal and at most one native close per view.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, a live webContents was checked and closed once; after the diff it is captured, checked, and closed once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The native close remains required on the explicit destruction critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One invocation per explicitly destroyed view; group context disposal iterates its view IDs sequentially, unchanged by this PR.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Group-owned context disposal serializes view removal/destruction; direct service calls have no new concurrency introduced by the guard.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No relevant cache. The browserViews map remains the ownership index and is removed on close as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the service call and disposal implementation are direct and unchanged except for the safe capture/null guard.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: View counts depend on usage, but before/after native-operation cardinality is identical.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; live-view disposal has the same native boundary count and effectively slightly fewer property accesses.

Scenarios.Scenario: BrowserView smoke test restarts the application and scans the main-process log for the prior disposal exception.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing `app.restart()` stops and relaunches the Code process. After restart completes, the added synchronous read loads `main.log` and the regex assertion scans it before page restoration checks proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stop and relaunch the Code application.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One stop/start pair for this smoke test.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The test already restarted the application once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Dominates the test restart critical path and must finish before the new log assertion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronously read the suite-scoped `main.log` in full.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One file read after the single restart, followed by one regex scan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No log file read or scan occurred at this point.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds O(log bytes) test-only work before restoration assertions; it is not on a product/user workflow.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly one log file read and one linear regex scan in the final test of this suite; cost scales with this suite's main.log byte size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The new read/scan is synchronous and serialized after restart; no parallelism or coalescing is relevant.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is used. The OS page cache may make the single read warm, but the test does not memoize it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the synchronous full-file read is introduced and on the test path; low evidence of material performance impact.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact log size varies by smoke-run verbosity, but the path is suite-scoped and read once; there is no evidence of a realistically large file or meaningful suite slowdown.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The added filesystem/allocation work is a one-time test assertion with no concrete material performance regression or user-visible impact.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and traced native disposal ownership, explicit destruction, restart boundaries, and the new log read. No actionable performance regression was introduced, and there was insufficient evidence to classify the correctness-focused cleanup fix as a concrete shipped performance-regression fix.
